text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Balochistan province Governor Imranullah Khan dissolved the provincial assembly and Mir Zafarullah Jamali was named as caretaker chief minister of the province.
- The Federal government has decided to dissolve the North West Frontier province assembly, removing the PDF coalition government within the next 24 hours.
- The caretaker government has turned down the request of the deposed prime minister Benazir Bhutto to again meet her detained husband Asif Ali Zardari, party sources said.
- Top-level changes in the financial sector, that include two biggest banks of the country, are being made next week for which a high-level meeting is expected either on Saturday or Sunday.

- Shahid Burki, the nominated adviser to the caretaker prime minister on finance and economic affairs, will meet the visiting IMF team on Saturday to finalise the on-going talks concerning the suspended Standby loan arrangement, sources said.
- The caretaker government is likely to set up a four member high powered accountability commission soon, official sources said.
- The caretaker government has started investigation against 150 dismissed bureaucrats employed by the previous government on contract, it was reliably learnt.
- Two top banks and several government-controlled financial institutions are showing alarming ratios of bad loans.

- The caretaker government has started looking for new avenues to generate funds and all the five major public sector corporations were being asked to urgently clear their dues to ease the current acute treasury position.
- Moody's has lowered the long term foreign currency deposit ratings of four Pakistani banks and announced that the rating will be kept on review for a possible further downgrade.
- Dumping by Chinese manufacturers, lack of incentives, high cost of production and freight charges have made the cement export unviable.
- The President of the World Bank James Wolfensohn has refused to release on leave Ishrat Hussain who was assigned an important position by the caretaker government in Islamabad.
- Deposed prime minister Benazir Bhutto continues to shore up support from law experts and political figures to launch a dauntless battle against her removal.
